info.title: AutoAir API
info.description: No-code DAG builder for Apache Airflow 3

get.description: What the sign-in page offers (no authentication needed).

The caller's Airflow session: a bearer token, else the Airflow UI cookie, verified
against Airflow (standalone). 401 when there is none or it is no longer valid — e.g.
after signing out of Airflow (the UI then signs AutoAir out too).

post.description:
Renew a cookie session through Airflow: any request carrying the cookie lets
Airflow's JWT refresh middleware re-issue it (auth managers with refreshable sessions,
e.g. Keycloak); the new cookie is passed on. Bearer tokens cannot be renewed (409).

401.description: The Airflow session has ended (cookie cleared).

get.description:
Readiness: the catalog, and (server.ready_check_storage / ready_check_airflow) the
deploy target and Airflow's health endpoint. 503 when a check fails.
The caller: user, AutoAir roles, effective permissions, deploy rights, auth mode.

parameters.name: team

schema.description: Deploy rights on this team's target (multi-team).
schema.title: Team

parameters.description: Deploy rights on this team's target (multi-team).

get.description:
What the catalog build scanned and found, what was filtered out and why, failed
modules and applied package metadata (catalog:refresh permission).

post.description: Create the connection in Airflow (the caller's Airflow permissions apply).

get.description:
Per conn_type form metadata (standard field labels/visibility, typed extra fields)
for the new-connection form; empty when Airflow does not provide it.

post.description: Send a (test) asset event: downstream asset-scheduled DAGs react to it.
Trigger the DAG that produces the asset (Airflow's own DAG run permission applies).

get.description:
Version-dependent run operations of the connected Airflow (falls back to the
installed Airflow's version when the server cannot be asked).

put.description: Pause / unpause in Airflow (the caller's token: Airflow enforces DAG edit rights).
Airflow >= 3.4: activate, drain or pause the DAG (PATCH scheduling_state).

post.description:
Check an environment's connection/variable mapping against the connected Airflow
(the Airflow AutoAir deploys that environment to). Never an error: ids can come from a
secrets backend the REST API cannot list.
Compute upcoming run times of the spec's schedule with Airflow's own timetable.
Token-streamed explanation (``text/event-stream``; result kind ``explain_code``).
Apply the patches of the selected findings and validate the result.

get.description: Hybrid retrieval over operators, docs, saved DAGs and templates.
Search installed provider docs / examples and the knowledge base (air-gapped).

post.description: Open-ended question answered by the tool-using agent (read-only tools).
The agent as a stream: tokens, tool calls/results, usage, then the ``agent`` result.

get.description: Writer kinds and the installed environment their prompts are built from.

post.description: Write code with a specialised writer (validate-and-repair loop).

Send a tiny prompt with the caller's effective model, or - with a body - with the
unsaved model settings of the form (validated like a save, never stored).

put.description: Upload a replacement of a built-in document, or a new custom document.

delete.description: Back to the default: delete the override and UI toggles (custom docs are removed).

post.description:
One assistant turn as a stream (tokens, tool calls/results, usage, then the
``assistant_turn`` result: the stored user + assistant messages).

Record that the user approved (applied in the editor), rejected or deployed a
proposal. Approving a spec change needs ``spec:write``.

get.description:
Connect to an allowed external MCP server and list its tools (allow-list applied).
The caller must be allowed to use ``agent`` (troubleshooting: airflow:read; admin
assistant: ai:admin or admin:panel).

post.description:
Analyse a DAG run as a stream (evidence collection, tool calls, tokens), ending with
the stored ``troubleshoot`` analysis. Read-only: proposals need an explicit decision.

Approve (returns the patched, validated spec and its generated code for the normal
deploy pipeline; needs ``spec:write``) or reject the analysis' proposed change.
Record that the approved change went through the deploy pipeline.

Execute (hitl: the user's approval of this one action; needs ``run:manage`` and
``features.runs``) or reject one proposed Airflow action of an analysis. Executing an
action that already succeeded or was skipped returns the analysis unchanged.

Airflow 2 → 3 idioms of one spec, some saved DAGs or all of them (ruff AIR3 + rules;
an LLM pass for a single DAG). Proposals come back as a reviewable diff.
A commit subject and PR description summarising the spec diff of a deploy.
ShellCheck diagnostics for a bash command/script (Jinja masked). Optional dependency.

Syntax/lint diagnostics of a code field with the best checker installed (ast + ruff,
strict JSON, YAML, bash -n + ShellCheck, sqlglot, gofmt, javac, tsc/esbuild). Nothing
is executed; the response says which tools ran or are missing.

get.description:
Which language servers are installed (the editor falls back to the built-in
completions for a missing one).

post.description: Ticket to open a language-server WebSocket for ``language``.

parameters.name: environment

schema.description: Render with this environment's overlay and connection/variable mapping applied (the read-only environment preview). Raw code DAGs render unchanged.
schema.title: Environment

parameters.description: Render with this environment's overlay and connection/variable mapping applied (the read-only environment preview). Raw code DAGs render unchanged.

post.description:
``environment`` (default: ``default_environment``) applies that environment's overlay
and selects the policy rules that match it.

Best-practice review by rules: retries, timeouts, idempotency, Airflow 3 idioms,
ownership and docs. Findings carry JSON patches; ``proposed_spec`` has them applied.

Leak scan by rules: hard-coded secrets, credentials exposed through logs, templates,
XCom or command lines, and unbounded resources. Secret values are masked.
Airflow 3.4 native YAML Dag (AIP-85).
Parses an AutoAir spec file (older spec versions are migrated).
Reverse-engineer a hand-written Python DAG file (runs in an isolated subprocess).

Code mode: import the edited DAG file into a spec (syntax checked first, then executed
in an isolated subprocess). Problems come back located when possible; nothing is saved.
Fetch an existing DAG's source from Airflow (``/dagSources``) and import it.

Import every DAG file of a repository with the Python importer (isolated subprocesses)
and report per file what was found, which DAGs convert and which already exist. Nothing
is saved: the client deploys the selected specs (``create_only``, or the stored etag for
a confirmed overwrite).

Create a template, or publish a new version of a saved one (operator templates get
the next version number; older versions stay readable under `/versions`).

post.description:
Approve, request changes on, or comment a spec version: a stored version or a deploy
proposal (by its etag). The author of a proposal cannot approve it.

get.description: Pending deploy proposals of a DAG (newest first).
A deploy proposal: the proposed spec, its reviews, and the stored spec (diff base).

post.description:
The commit message / pull request description a deploy of ``body`` would produce
(nothing is written; the validation is static).

Deploy an approved proposal. Anyone holding ``deploy`` may, including its author,
once another user approved it.

post.description:
Open a promotion pull request. With AutoAir's services (not in a bare router) the
commit/PR carry the deploy context, the git token typed for this request (header
X-AutoAir-Git-Token, storage.git.request_token) or the user's own git credentials
(per_user mode) are used, and the promotion is audited (autoair.governance).

post.description: Short-lived ticket to join the DAG's live editing room (needs DAG edit permission).

get.description: Current deploy target and the options this Airflow offers (bundles, git checkout).

put.description:
Test, persist (secrets excluded — use an Airflow connection) and switch now. The
administrator's policy (allowed target kinds, forced git connection, credential rules)
is enforced: disallowed kinds are refused, policy fields are taken from configuration.

delete.description: Forget the target chosen in the UI and go back to AUTOAIR_STORAGE__* settings.

get.description:
Which credentials the caller's git deploys use: a token typed per deploy
(storage.git.request_token), the forced or shared connection, or their own connection
(per-user credentials, looked up with their token so Airflow's RBAC applies).
Entries of every configured source (signature-verified indexes only).

post.description: Downloads a template/fragment, checks its SHA-256 against the signed index, saves it.

get.description: Every effective setting with its source, type, default and description.
Versions, backends, feature flags, replicas and catalog statistics.
The audit trail, newest first, filtered (``since`` inclusive, ``until`` exclusive).

The filtered audit trail as CSV (formula-like cells are neutralised). ``limit``
defaults to ``admin.export_default`` and may not exceed ``admin.export_limit``.
Every template (built-in and saved), saved ones first.
Users seen by this AutoAir (their AutoAir roles when last seen) and in the audit.
Requests, tokens and cost per user and model over the last ``days`` (AI audit log).
Pending deploy proposals of every DAG and recent review verdicts.
State backend, schema version, pending migrations and table sizes.

post.description: Apply pending schema migrations (like ``autoair db upgrade``).

get.description: In-process caches of this replica (each replica has its own).

post.description:
Rebuild the catalog, forget marketplace indexes or rebuild the AI index (this
replica).

get.description: Every feature flag: configured value, runtime override, effective value, lock.

put.description: Set (``value``) or remove (``null``) the runtime override of one flag.

get.description: Every external MCP server (configuration and admin panel), secrets hidden.

post.description: Connect and list the server's tools (with whether the allow-list permits each).

get.description: Index size, store, search mode, sources and the last / running refresh.
Hybrid search (BM25 + embeddings, RRF, optional reranker) with citations.

put.description: Override a configured source at runtime (enabled, components, versions).

delete.description: Drop the admin-panel override of a source (back to the configuration).

post.description: Start a refresh or rebuild in the background (409 while one runs anywhere).
Ask the running refresh to stop (it keeps what it indexed).

get.description: Download the index as a KB bundle (zip, unsigned; sign with `autoair kb build`).

post.description:
Import a KB bundle (request body: the zip; bound by server.max_body_bytes - use
`autoair kb import` for larger bundles). Checksums are verified, signatures when
kb.bundle.public_keys is set.

api_url.description: REST API base URL (GitHub Enterprise, self-hosted GitLab, Azure DevOps Server…); default: the public host's. gitea: default <scheme>://<host>/api/v1 of an http(s) repo URL (required for SSH remotes).

use_airflow_bundle.title: Use Airflow Bundle
use_airflow_bundle.description: Fill repo/branch/subdir/credentials from Airflow's GitDagBundle config.

bundle_name.title: Bundle Name
bundle_name.description: GitDagBundle to read (use_airflow_bundle; default: the first).

credentials_ttl.title: Credentials Ttl
credentials_ttl.description: Seconds the credentials read from an Airflow connection (conn_id, forced_conn_id, the bundle's or a user's own) are reused before the connection is read again; on an authentication failure it is re-read at once and the operation retried, so a rotated token works without a restart. 0 = read on every operation.

fetch_interval.title: Fetch Interval
fetch_interval.description: provider=local: seconds between fetches of the remote.

direct_push_roles.title: Direct Push Roles
direct_push_roles.description: AutoAir roles allowed to push straight to the target branch (deploy request flag direct_push=true in mode=pr; see iam.force_pr_without_direct_push for mode=push). Evaluated by autoair.iam; unset = iam.direct_push_roles applies (default ['Admin']); [] = nobody, except users granted 'deploy:direct_push' explicitly.

forced_conn_id.title: Forced Conn Id
forced_conn_id.description: Admin policy: the Airflow connection every git deploy uses. Overrides conn_id (and the bundle's connection); the deploy-target dialog cannot change it.

credentials_mode.title: Credentials Mode
credentials_mode.description: shared: one service connection/token for everybody; per_user: commits and pull requests use the deploying user's own Airflow connection (see user_conn_id_template), read with the user's token so Airflow's RBAC applies. Reads (listing, history) keep the shared credentials when configured.

user_conn_id_template.title: User Conn Id Template
user_conn_id_template.description: per_user: the user's connection id. Placeholders: {username} (the Airflow username, lower-cased; characters outside [A-Za-z0-9_.-] become '_').

user_conn_id_pattern.title: User Conn Id Pattern
user_conn_id_pattern.description: per_user: regex (fullmatch) of connection ids a user may pick in the deploy dialog instead of the template's (e.g. 'git_.*'); unset: only the template.

user_credentials_fallback.title: User Credentials Fallback
user_credentials_fallback.description: per_user: use the shared credentials when the user has no readable connection (otherwise such deploys are refused).

request_token.title: Request Token
request_token.description: Git token the user types for one deploy, delete, promotion or pull request (header X-AutoAir-Git-Token, never stored, logged or audited): off = the header is refused; optional = a token, when given, replaces the configured credentials for that one write; required = every git write needs one (the configured connection, if any, only serves reads; MCP git writes need mcp_request_token and the header). A team target uses its own team_storage.<team>.git.request_token, but off here turns request tokens off for every target. With forced_conn_id set, tokens are refused unless request_token_overrides_forced.

request_token_overrides_forced.title: Request Token Overrides Forced
request_token_overrides_forced.description: A request token may replace the admin-forced connection (forced_conn_id) for that one write. Default: the forced connection always wins and the X-AutoAir-Git-Token header is refused.

mcp_request_token.title: Mcp Request Token
mcp_request_token.description: MCP over HTTP: save_dag_spec / delete_dag_spec take the user's git token from the X-AutoAir-Git-Token header of the MCP request (set in the MCP client's server configuration; never a tool argument, so it stays out of the model's context and transcripts). request_token, the forced-connection rule and the HTTPS rule apply as for the REST API. Off: such a header is refused.

request_token_allow_insecure.title: Request Token Allow Insecure
request_token_allow_insecure.description: Accept X-AutoAir-Git-Token over plain HTTP from a non-loopback client (the scheme and client address honour server.proxy_headers / forwarded_allow_ips), and send it to http:// git hosts. Only for test setups.

commit_author.title: Commit Author
commit_author.description: Commit author: service = the service identity (the user is credited in trailers and Co-authored-by); user = the deploying user ('Name <email>'); auto = user with per_user credentials, else service. GitHub's API always commits as the token's owner (the user is credited with Co-authored-by).

commit_message_template.title: Commit Message Template
commit_message_template.description: Commit message of a save without a user message. Placeholders: {dag_id}, {environment}, {author} and the context placeholders ({user}, {user_name}, {user_email}, {autoair_version}, {etag_before}, {etag_after}, {validation}, {approvals}, {link}, {target}, {description}, {context}). The context block and trailers are always appended unless the template places {context} itself.

pr_title_template.title: Pr Title Template
